name: Sicilian Defense
summary: Meet 1.e4 with ...c5 and fight for d4 from the flank. Learn a Classical Open Sicilian setup and practical replies to the Alapin, Closed Sicilian and Rossolimo, with explanations of both sides' plans.

chunks.title: Introduction: Fight for d4
chunks.summary: Understand what ...c5 achieves before learning a setup. The central exchange opens a file and gives both sides different strengths.
keyIdeas: ...c5 controls d4, but does not attack the pawn on e4 directly.
After d4 cxd4 Nxd4, Black has a half-open c-file; White has quick development and more space.
This repertoire uses 2...Nc6. After 3.Bb5, use the Rossolimo lesson rather than following the Open Sicilian line automatically.

plans.white: Develop quickly, support e4 and look for central or kingside activity. Black's uncastled king may matter if the position opens early.
plans.black: Develop and secure the king before using the c-file. Prepare ...d5 only when the center and king can withstand the exchanges.

line.note: White claims central space and opens the f1 bishop.
Controls d4 with a flank pawn. Black creates an asymmetric position rather than matching e4 with ...e5.

comparison.explanation: 1...e5 is a sound classical defense, but creates a different pawn structure and opens the f8 bishop immediately. ...c5 instead contests d4 from the side; it is a repertoire choice, not a refutation of ...e5.

line.note: Develops toward the center and prepares d4.
Develops the b8 knight and adds control of d4. This move order also allows White's Bb5 Rossolimo.
White challenges the center, offering a central pawn for Black's c-pawn.
Exchanges the c-pawn for White's d-pawn. Black gets a half-open c-file and retains both central pawns, while White gains room for active pieces.

checkpoint.prompt: If you exchange c5 for d4, which file becomes half-open for Black, and what does White gain?
checkpoint.answer: The c-file becomes half-open for Black. White gains an active knight on d4 and quick development, so Black should not start attacking before bringing out the pieces.

line.note: White recaptures with an active knight rather than bringing the queen out.
Develops with an attack on e4. White must account for that threat, usually by defending with Nc3.

questions.prompt: You're Black. Start the Sicilian by controlling d4 with a flank pawn.
questions.explanation: 1...c5 contests d4 without mirroring e4. Unlike ...e5, it leaves Black's e-pawn flexible, but does not free the f8 bishop yet.

questions.prompt: White developed Nf3. Develop your queenside knight and reinforce d4 in this repertoire.
questions.explanation: 2...Nc6 develops and controls d4. ...d6 and ...e6 are also sound Sicilian move orders; this course uses ...Nc6 and covers the Bb5 reply it permits.

questions.prompt: White played d4. Exchange your flank pawn for the central pawn.
questions.hint: The c5 pawn can capture on d4.
questions.explanation: 3...cxd4 exchanges the c-pawn for White's d-pawn. Black gains a half-open c-file, but White gets active development after Nxd4. Neither benefit is a forced advantage.

chunks.title: Open Sicilian: Classical Development
chunks.summary: Use ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and ...d6, then develop the bishop and castle. Learn a sound setup against Be2 without treating it as an answer to every White system.
keyIdeas: ...Nf6 attacks e4; ...d6 controls e5 and opens the c8 bishop's diagonal.
...e6 covers d5 and prepares ...Be7, but restricts the c8 bishop and concedes some space.
White's Be2 setup is quieter than Bg5 or Bc4. Those alternatives require fresh decisions, not automatic moves.

plans.white: Develop the queen and rooks, assess f4 or a central advance, and keep d4 and e4 sufficiently defended.
plans.black: Consider ...Bd7, ...Qc7 and ...Rc8 as the position allows. The freeing ...d5 break needs enough support; do not weaken d6 or expose the king to force it.

line.note: White claims central space and opens the f1 bishop.
Controls d4 with a flank pawn. Black creates an asymmetric position rather than matching e4 with ...e5.
Develops toward the center and prepares d4.
Develops the b8 knight and adds control of d4. This move order also allows White's Bb5 Rossolimo.
White challenges the center, offering a central pawn for Black's c-pawn.
Exchanges the c-pawn for White's d-pawn. Black gets a half-open c-file and retains both central pawns, while White gains room for active pieces.
White recaptures with an active knight rather than bringing the queen out.
Develops with an attack on e4. White must account for that threat, usually by defending with Nc3.
Defends e4 and develops another piece. White is ready to choose a system against Black's setup.
Controls e5 and opens the c8 bishop's diagonal. Black prepares piece development while keeping the e-pawn flexible.

checkpoint.prompt: Before trying to use the c-file, what central square and undeveloped bishop can one pawn move help?
checkpoint.answer: ...d6 covers e5 and opens the c8 bishop's diagonal. Development and king safety make the later c-file pressure useful.

line.note: White chooses a quieter developing square and prepares castling.
Covers d5 and opens the f8 bishop's route to e7. This small-center setup leaves Black flexible but temporarily restricts the c8 bishop.

comparison.explanation: 6...g6 would choose a Dragon-style fianchetto. ...e6 instead supports d5 and develops the bishop through e7. Each setup has different attacking patterns; do not mix them without considering the pawn structure.

line.note: White secures the king before central play.
Develops the f8 bishop and clears the way to castle. The bishop is modestly placed but helps complete king safety.
White develops the remaining bishop and connects the pieces.
Secures the king before seeking play on the c-file or a central break.

questions.prompt: White has recaptured on d4. Develop while attacking e4.
questions.hint: The g8 knight can attack the e-pawn.
questions.explanation: 4...Nf6 develops with a concrete threat to e4. White commonly answers Nc3. The move ...d6 is also a sound order, but does not itself attack e4.

questions.prompt: White defended e4 with Nc3. Control e5 and open your c8 bishop's diagonal.
questions.explanation: 5...d6 controls e5 and frees the c8 bishop. It leads to the Classical Sicilian here. ...e6 is another sound system, but changes the setup and move order.

questions.prompt: White has castled. Develop your f8 bishop to prepare your own castling.
questions.explanation: 7...Be7 finishes the piece development needed for O-O. Plans involving ...Rc8 or ...d5 become safer once the king is secure.

chunks.title: Alapin: Challenge the Center Immediately
chunks.summary: Against 2.c3, play ...d5 while Nc3 is unavailable. Learn why an early queen recapture is playable in this specific position.
keyIdeas: c3 prepares d4 but occupies the knight's natural developing square.
...d5 challenges e4 before White can establish the full center unopposed.
After exd5 Qxd5, White cannot chase the queen with Nc3 while its own pawn remains on c3. That explains the timing, but does not make the queen immune to attack.

plans.white: Complete development, then decide how to maintain or resolve the d4/c5 tension. Look for useful attacks on the queen only when they also improve pieces.
plans.black: Finish development and choose the timing of ...cxd4. If White recaptures cxd4, play against the resulting isolated d-pawn without neglecting White's activity.

line.note: White occupies the center.
Black contests d4 with the c-pawn.
Prepares d4 with pawn support but blocks the b1 knight's c3 square.
Challenges e4 immediately. Black uses the moment when White cannot develop Nc3 with an attack on a queen recapturing on d5.

comparison.explanation: 2...Nc6 is playable, but lets White build d4 without the immediate ...d5 challenge. Our ...d5 uses the temporary absence of Nc3 to clarify the center; ...Nf6 is also a major choice.

line.note: White exchanges the e-pawn for Black's d-pawn, opening the central files.
Restores material with the queen. Nc3 cannot currently gain time against her because White's c-pawn occupies c3.

checkpoint.prompt: Why is a queen recapture on d5 less exposed here than after White has already played Nc3?
checkpoint.answer: White's own c3 pawn blocks Nb1–c3. Black can restore material with ...Qxd5 without allowing that developing attack immediately.

line.note: White gains central space and attacks c5, completing the point of c3.
Develops a knight, controls d5 and e4, and prepares castling. Black can keep central pawn tension for now.
White develops and prepares castling while the central pawns remain in tension.
Releases the f8 bishop and covers d5. The queen on d5 defends c5; the e6 pawn itself does not. Black chooses a solid development setup.
White clears f1 for castling and supports a safe central buildup.
Develops the bishop and makes castling available.
White secures the king.
Black also secures the king; future ...cxd4 exchanges can change the pawn structure.

questions.prompt: White's c3 prepares d4 but blocks Nc3. Challenge e4 right away.
questions.explanation: 2...d5 attacks e4 immediately. After exd5, ...Qxd5 is viable because White cannot develop Nc3 while c3 is occupied. ...Nf6 is another major Alapin response.

questions.prompt: White exchanged on d5. Recover the pawn without moving either knight.
questions.hint: The queen has a clear d-file.
questions.explanation: 3...Qxd5 restores material. Unlike many early queen moves, it cannot be chased immediately by Nc3 because White's c-pawn is on c3. Continue development and remain alert to later queen attacks.

questions.prompt: After both kingside knights develop, cover d5 and release the f8 bishop.
questions.explanation: 5...e6 opens the f8 bishop and covers d5. It does not defend c5: the queen on d5 does that. Black prepares ...Be7 and castling before deciding when to exchange on d4.

chunks.title: Closed Sicilian: Develop Before Expanding
chunks.summary: Against Nc3 and g3, develop with a kingside fianchetto. White has postponed d4, so adapt to a slower struggle.
keyIdeas: Nc3 does not force a closed game: White can still play d4 later. Read the next moves.
...g6 and ...Bg7 develop the bishop on a long diagonal; ...d6 supports c5 and opens Bc8.
Queenside expansion with ...b5 needs preparation and timing. White's f4 can start kingside play while Black develops.

plans.white: Use the extra kingside space to improve the pieces and assess f5. If d4 becomes attractive, calculate how opening the center changes the bishops' activity.
plans.black: Develop Bc8, consider ...Rb8 and a supported ...b5, and watch White's f5 ideas. A timely ...d5 can challenge the center, but needs preparation.

line.note: White takes central space.
Black contests d4 from the flank.
White develops and keeps the option of either d4 or a slower closed setup.
Develops and reinforces d4. Black does not yet have to commit the e-pawn.
White prepares Bg2, signaling a slower kingside fianchetto.
Prepares ...Bg7 so the bishop can influence the long diagonal toward the queenside.
White places the bishop on the long diagonal behind the e4 pawn.
Develops the bishop and clears f8 for castling once the knight moves. The diagonal may open as the central pawns change.
Supports e4 and releases White's c1 bishop.
Supports c5 and opens Black's c8 bishop's diagonal. Black keeps a firm grip on the flank pawn before expanding.
White gains kingside space and may prepare f5. Black needs counterplay as well as king safety.
Covers d5 and clears e7 for the g8 knight. The cost is restricting the c8 bishop again until the pawn structure opens.
White develops toward castling and reinforces the center.
Develops to e7, keeping the g7–f6–e5 diagonal free of a knight on f6. It also leaves the f-pawn available; assess tactics before advancing it.

comparison.explanation: 7...Nf6 is natural and sound. Nge7 keeps f6 clear and avoids giving a future e5 advance a knight target on f6. The tradeoff is a more modest knight square.

checkpoint.prompt: Which knight move prepares castling without giving White's future e5 advance a target on f6?
checkpoint.answer: ...Nge7 develops and keeps the f-pawn flexible. It is a setup choice, not a claim that ...Nf6 loses.

line.note: White secures the king and may continue a kingside buildup.
Black secures the king. Queenside play must now be coordinated with the pieces rather than launched automatically.

questions.prompt: White prepares Bg2. Prepare your own bishop for the long diagonal.
questions.explanation: 3...g6 prepares ...Bg7, choosing a coordinated fianchetto setup. ...e6 is also sound but would lead to a different development plan.

questions.prompt: Your bishop's path is open. Complete the fianchetto.
questions.explanation: 4...Bg7 develops the bishop toward the queenside and prepares king safety. The bishop's scope depends on central pawn exchanges; it is not a ready-made attack.

questions.prompt: With e7 available, develop the g8 knight to keep the f-pawn flexible.
questions.hint: Use e7 rather than f6 in this setup.
questions.explanation: 7...Nge7 prepares castling and leaves the f-pawn free. ...Nf6 is another sound setup, but can face e5 with tempo when White has prepared it.

chunks.title: Rossolimo: The Bishop Pair Has a Cost
chunks.summary: Meet 3.Bb5 with ...g6. If White exchanges on c6, understand the doubled pawns and bishop pair instead of calling either an automatic advantage.
keyIdeas: Bb5 is a response to the ...Nc6 move order. It is not the Open Sicilian, so White need not play d4.
After Bxc6 dxc6, Black has doubled c-pawns and the bishop pair. Open lines can help the bishops; pawn weaknesses can help White.
...dxc6 opens the c8 bishop's diagonal and the d-file. The remaining c5 pawn still contests d4.

plans.white: Develop Bc1 and Nb1, assess the timing of d4, and pressure the doubled pawns without underestimating Black's bishops.
plans.black: Develop Bc8 and seek active lines for both bishops. Keep c5 defended and consider central exchanges before White fixes the queenside weaknesses.

line.note: White occupies e4 and opens the bishop's diagonal.
Black controls d4 with a flank pawn.
White develops and prepares central play.
Develops and controls d4, allowing White to choose the Bb5 Rossolimo.
Attacks Nc6 and offers a structural decision: preserve the knight or allow bishop-for-knight exchange.
Prepares the f8 bishop's fianchetto rather than spending time defending the knight with a pawn move.
White gives up the bishop pair to damage Black's queenside pawns.
Recaptures with the d-pawn, opening the c8 bishop's diagonal and d-file. Black accepts doubled c-pawns in exchange for the two bishops.

comparison.explanation: 4...bxc6 is playable too: it keeps the d-pawn and opens the b-file, but gives a different structure. Our ...dxc6 opens Bc8's diagonal immediately and is chosen for that plan.

checkpoint.prompt: What do you gain and concede by recapturing on c6 with the d-pawn?
checkpoint.answer: Black keeps two bishops and opens Bc8's diagonal, but accepts doubled c-pawns. Plan around both features rather than assuming the exchange favored one side automatically.

line.note: Supports e4 and opens White's remaining bishop.
Develops the bishop toward the center and queenside. Black should seek positions where the bishop pair has room.
White secures the king before building pressure against the pawns.
Develops and attacks e4, which d3 already defends. Black is completing king safety rather than winning a pawn by force.
White reinforces e4 and places a rook on a central file.
Secures the king. Now Black can develop the c8 bishop and coordinate counterplay.

questions.prompt: White chose Bb5 instead of d4. Prepare a kingside fianchetto.
questions.hint: The g-pawn can open g7 for the bishop.
questions.explanation: 3...g6 prepares ...Bg7 and accepts that White may exchange on c6. ...e6 is also a sound Rossolimo setup; do not automatically copy an Open Sicilian line.

questions.prompt: White traded its bishop for Nc6. Recapture with the d-pawn to open Bc8's diagonal.
questions.hint: The d7 pawn can capture c6.
questions.explanation: 4...dxc6 accepts doubled c-pawns and preserves the bishop pair. ...bxc6 is also playable but gives a different pawn structure. Neither doubled pawns nor two bishops decide the game alone.

questions.prompt: You prepared g7 for the f8 bishop. Develop it now.
questions.explanation: 5...Bg7 develops a bishop rather than spending more time on pawns. The bishop pair needs open lines and coordinated pieces to become useful.
